adaptations: The source vendor fixture (SDK0.5.12 and exact146.0.7680.177.5 target) is represented by the typed Vendor trait. Native production uses the ported0.7.2 protocol, whose no-key/latest-only acquisition is unavailable without an existing exact pin and eligible vendor key; it never claims or purchases a key.

Launch preparation returns the environment owned by the future child (AUTO_UPDATE=false and the pinned existing binary), instead of changing process-global Python environment. Assertions cover the returned environment and preserve zero download calls.
Native production defaults the cache to the selected data root/browser-cache/cloak, honoring explicit vendor cache/binary overrides. Reading an offer creates no vendor cache or home files.

The shared-cache process case re-enters only its own named Rust test in a real independently captured child process. It executes the production Acquisition/cache-wide SessionLease and exits9 on WouldBlock before the vendor boundary; no additional reported test ID or Python helper is introduced.

The CLI/HTTP case calls the real parser/reflection/engines-command seam and real HTTP router. Its injected Service replaces only vendor/helper IO, matching the original run_cli seam; approval, exact-body, stale-offer, token-policy and admission decisions remain production code.
The separately ported three routes_acquisition source IDs are owned by the source_http suite and are not counted in this nine-case suite.

cases.fault: missing binary; zero vendor calls and no cache creation
decline, wrong/stale exact offer and approval replay; cached launch never downloads
user-owned binary override and missing override remain acquisition-disabled
unpinned key or custom mirror cannot reach vendor downloader
free/latest-only license refused before exact download; eligible paid exact pin passes
same-process reentrant acquisition hits real cache-wide OS lease
independent child acquisition refuses parent's real vendor-cache lease before downloader
injected vendor OSError preserves failure and releases its lease so retry succeeds
actual CLI offer equals HTTP; decline400/stale409 make no calls; approval200 has exact target
